args.rationale: Applying the operative rule memo (Whitlock & Deene LLP, Civil Procedure Group, personal jurisdiction and diversity jurisdiction tests) to Scenario 2 of the Ostrander Tooling Works intake letter: the proposed Ohio court suit against Brumfeld Freight Lines (a Georgia carrier) fails the personal jurisdiction test on both prongs of specific jurisdiction. Purposeful contacts: Brumfeld has no operations, customers, employees, or solicitation in Ohio; its only Ohio connection is a single driver who once passed through Ohio in transit on a Pennsylvania-to-Kentucky route unrelated to the claim. Under the memo, merely fortuitous transit on unrelated business does not constitute purposeful availment. Nexus: the claim (a loading-dock injury to Ostrander's purchasing agent) arose entirely at Brumfeld's Savannah, Georgia terminal during a site visit and bears no relation to any Ohio forum contact. General jurisdiction also fails because Brumfeld is not domiciled in Ohio. Per the firm rule of decision in the memo, a defendant with no operations, customers, or purposeful activity in the forum whose only connection is unrelated transit satisfies neither prong, so an Ohio court lacks personal jurisdiction. Determination: rejected.
